unit_title: Unit 2: Speculations About the Future of Science - Grammar Focus (Future Tenses)
content: Unit 2: Grammar Focus - Future Tenses & Reading Analysis (Communicative English Skills II - EnLa102) ========================================= 1. CORE CONCEPTS AND FUNDAMENTALS OF FUTURE TENSES ========================================= What is Future Tense in English Grammar? In English grammar, future time is expressed through various verb forms depending on the speaker's intention, degree of certainty, planning, or immediate evidence. Unlike past or present tenses, there is no single morphological 'future tense' verb form; instead, we use modal auxiliaries like will, semi-modals like be going to, or present tenses (Present Continuous and Simple Present) with future meaning. A. Expressing Future with 'Will' (Simple Future): Used for spontaneous decisions made at the moment of speaking, predictions based on personal opinions/beliefs, promises, offers, and unalterable future facts. Formula: Subject + will + Base Verb (V1) Example: I will call you as soon as I get the research report. - Amharic: ላላቀድነውና በወቅቱ ለምንወስነው ውሳኔ፣ ለቃል ኪዳን፣ እንዲሁም በግል አስተያየት ላይ ለተመሰረተ ግምት ያገለግላል። B. Expressing Future with 'Be Going To': Used for prior plans, intentions made before the moment of speaking, and predictions based on present physical evidence. Formula: Subject + am/is/are + going to + Base Verb (V1) Example: Look at those dark clouds; it is going to rain. - Amharic: ከዚህ ቀደም ለታቀደ እቅድ እና በአሁኑ ወቅት በሚታይ ግልጽ ማስረጃ ላይ የተመሰረተ ግምትን ለመግለጽ ያገለግላል። C. Expressing Future with Present Continuous: Used for fixed arrangements in the near future involving specific time, place, or other people. Formula: Subject + am/is/are + Verb-ing Example: Dr. Aklilu is meeting the research team at 4:00 PM tomorrow. - Amharic: ቀን፣ ቦታ እና ሰዓት የተቆረጠላቸው የፀኑ የወደፊት ዝግጅቶችን (Fixed Arrangements) ለመግለጽ ያገለግላል። D. Expressing Future with Simple Present: Used for fixed timetables, official programs, and scheduled events beyond individual control. Formula: Subject + Verb 1 / Verb (s/es) Example: The scientific conference begins at 8:30 AM on Monday. - Amharic: በቋሚ የጊዜ ሰሌዳ (Timetables and Schedules) የተወሰኑ የወደፊት ድርጊቶችን ለመግለጽ ያገለግላል። ========================================= 2. COMPREHENSIVE TENSE MATRIX, FORMULAS AND EXAMPLES ========================================= A. Simple Future Tense (Will) Usage: Instant decisions, predictions without present evidence, promises, threats, and future facts. Active Affirmative: Subject + will + Verb 1 + Object Active Negative: Subject + will not (won't) + Verb 1 + Object Active Question: Will + Subject + Verb 1 + Object? Time Indicators: tomorrow, next week, in the future, soon, probably, I think, I believe. Examples: - Spontaneous Decision: I am bored. I will take a short break. - Promise: I will pay you back tomorrow. - Opinion Prediction: I think you will enjoy reading about Dr. Aklilu's research. - Future Fact: The sun will rise at 6:00 AM tomorrow. B. Be Going To Usage: Intentions, pre-planned actions, predictions based on present observable evidence. Active Affirmative: Subject + am/is/are + going to + Verb 1 + Object Active Negative: Subject + am/is/are + not + going to + Verb 1 + Object Active Question: Am/Is/Are + Subject + going to + Verb 1 + Object? Time Indicators: tonight, tomorrow, this weekend, look!, watch out!. Examples: - Intention/Plan: I am going to start eating healthier foods. - Present Evidence: Be careful! You are going to spill your tea! C. Present Continuous for Future Arrangements Usage: Confirmed personal arrangements, travel schedules, pre-booked events. Active Affirmative: Subject + am/is/are + Verb-ing + Object Active Negative: Subject + am/is/are + not + Verb-ing + Object Active Question: Am/Is/Are + Subject + Verb-ing + Object? Examples: - Arrangement: We are seeing the orchestra at 7:00 PM tonight. - Negative Arrangement: Rick is not attending the meeting tomorrow. D. Simple Present for Timetables Usage: Official schedules, public transit timetables, academic calendars. Active Affirmative: Subject + Verb 1 (s/es) + Object Active Negative: Subject + do/does not + Verb 1 + Object Active Question: Do/Does + Subject + Verb 1 + Object? Examples: - Timetable: The train leaves in five minutes. - Academic Schedule: Academic activities do not begin until February. ========================================= 3. READING PASSAGE ANALYSIS & VOCABULARY SOLUTIONS ========================================= Passage Overview: 'Grassroots Attack on Bilharzia' The reading text explores the scientific breakthrough by Ethiopian scientist Dr. Aklilu Lemma regarding Bilharzia (Schistosomiasis) control using Endod (Phytolacca dodecandra). Bilharzia is a parasitic disease affecting over 250 million people, transmitted via water snails (intermediate hosts). Dr. Lemma discovered that ground berries of Endod act as a potent, low-cost, natural molluscicide that kills snails without harming the environment or mammals. Vocabulary Matching Solutions (Activity 2.6 / Vocabulary Section): 1. It occasionally happens that a change in concentration affects the chemical action... -> dilution / toxicity 2. This acute infection of the brain is almost similarly fatal. -> invariably 3. What we're accomplishing with Howie is important; we can't stop doing it. -> vital 4. That is the deceptive nature of gambling that must be controlled. -> insidious 5. The teacher felt she needed to give out compliments to each student... -> dispense 6. The public work suffers from the consequences of white ants. -> ravages / afflictions ========================================= 4. TEXTBOOK ACTIVITY SOLUTIONS AND EXTENDED EXPLANATIONS ========================================= Activity 2.8: Grammar Analysis (Page 26) 1. What are future tenses? - Answer: Future tenses are verb forms and structures used in English to express actions, events, predictions, or states that will occur after the moment of speaking. 2. What are the different forms of future tenses? - Answer: Simple Future (will), Be going to, Present Continuous for planned arrangements, and Simple Present for timetables/schedules. 3. Underlined Future Tense Indicators in 'The Mystery Guest' Passage (Pages 26-27): - are going to have, will Grandma visit, is not going to visit, Is Uncle Bill going to stay, is not going to stay, is going to arrive, is going to stay, will she sleep, is going to sleep, will have, is going to visit, is going to have, are going to have, is going to be, am going to have, are going to love. Activity 2.9: 'A Wonderful Plan' Passage Completion (Pages 28-30) 1. In fact, they are arriving / are going to arrive at the airport in about an hour! 2. "Okay, so are we going to the concert tonight, right?" Nate asks. 3. "Are we going to the museum tomorrow, then?" her brother asks. 4. "Yes, I am leaving in five minutes," Allison says. 5. "What do you mean? We are both going, right?" 6. "No, silly! No one is coming to help us clean." 7. Now Nate is getting really nervous. 8. "Remember that you stay / are staying here, little brother..." 9. "...I am going out to have fun with Mom and Dad..." 10. "...and you stay / are staying here to clean the whole apartment..." Activity 2.10: Sara's Schedule (Page 31) 1. On Monday morning, Sara is going to have a doctor's appointment. In the afternoon, she is going to buy groceries for the week. In the evening, she is going to watch a movie with Dave. 2. On Tuesday morning, she is going to meet with her boss. In the afternoon, she is going to go to the gym. In the evening, she is going to do work reports. 3. On Wednesday morning, she is going to return library books. In the afternoon, she is going to go to the gym. In the evening, she is going to have dinner with girlfriends. 4. On Thursday morning and afternoon, she is going to attend a conference. In the evening, she is going to do the ironing. 5. On Friday morning, she is going to go to the gym. In the afternoon, she is going to buy food for the party. In the evening, she is going to have dinner with parents. Activity 2.11: Complete using 'going to' + Verb (Page 31) 1. My house is very dirty. I am going to clean it tomorrow. 2. Miriam is going to a party next Saturday. She is going to wear her new red dress. 3. Robert bought a new painting at the art show. He is going to hang it over the sofa in his living room. 4. The hockey championship is next month. The boys are going to practice every night next week. 5. Jack hates his job. He is going to quit next week. Activity 2.12: Predictions/Consequences with 'will + inf.' (Pages 31-32) 1. It's raining. Worku doesn't have an umbrella. - Answer: He will probably get wet. / He probably won't stay dry. 2. Zinash has a very bad cold. - Answer: She will probably stay in bed. / She probably won't go to class. 3. Sileshi didn't sleep well last night. - Answer: He will probably feel tired today. / He won't concentrate well. 4. Elias loves movies. There is a new movie playing at the theater tonight. - Answer: He will probably go to the theater tonight. 5. Selamawit ate too much dessert last night and now she has a stomachache. - Answer: She probably won't eat dessert tonight. / She will take some medicine. ========================================= 5. ADVANCED GRAMMAR RULES, EXAM TRICKS AND PITFALLS ========================================= Trick 1: Future Time Clauses Rule (ከጊዜ አያያዥ ቃላት በኋላ 'will' አይገባም) In time clauses introduced by when, before, after, as soon as, until, unless, if, do NOT use 'will' or 'be going to'. Use Simple Present Tense instead to express future time. Incorrect: I will call you when I will arrive at the university. Correct: I will call you when I arrive at the university. Amharic Explanation: ከጊዜ አያያዥ ቃላት (`when`, `as soon as`, `before`) በኋላ የሚከተለው አረፍተ ነገር በ Simple Present መጻፍ አለበት። `will` መጠቀም ፈጽሞ ስህተት ነው። Trick 2: Physical Evidence vs. Personal Opinion If present visual or sensory evidence exists, use be going to. If it is based on personal opinion, belief, or guess (using I think, I hope, probably), use will. Incorrect (with visual evidence): Look at that speed boat! It will crash! Correct: Look at that speed boat! It is going to crash! Trick 3: Instant Decision vs. Pre-planned Intention Decision made at the moment of speech -> will. Decision made prior to the moment of speech -> be going to. Example: A: "The phone is ringing." B: "I will answer it." (Instant decision) Example: A: "Why did you buy paint?" B: "I am going to paint my room." (Prior intention) Trick 4: Official Timetable vs. Personal Arrangement Public schedules (trains, exams, flights) -> Simple Present. Personal agreed appointments -> Present Continuous. Example: The plane takes off at 7:00 AM. (Timetable) Example: I am flying to Gondar tomorrow morning. (Personal arrangement) ========================================= 6. PRACTICE EXAM QUESTIONS WITH DETAILED EXPLANATIONS ========================================= Question 1: A: "Why have you collected all those laboratory test tubes?" B: "Because I ________ an experiment on Endod extract toxicity later today." A. will perform B. am going to perform C. perform D. performed Correct Answer: B. am going to perform Explanation: collecting test tubes beforehand proves that this action is a pre-planned intention (Prior Intention), so 'be going to' is required. Question 2: Watch out! That laboratory beaker ________ off the table! A. will fall B. falls C. is going to fall D. fallen Correct Answer: C. is going to fall Explanation: 'Watch out!' indicates immediate physical evidence happening right now, requiring 'be going to' for prediction based on current evidence. Question 3: Please send me the Bilharzia research paper as soon as the author ________ it. A. will finish B. finishes C. is going to finish D. finished Correct Answer: B. finishes Explanation: The conjunction 'as soon as' introduces a future time clause, which strictly requires Simple Present Tense ('finishes'), never 'will'. Question 4: According to the official university schedule, the second semester final exams ________ on Monday. A. start B. will start C. are going to start D. started Correct Answer: A. start Explanation: Official institution timetables and fixed schedules use the Simple Present Tense ('start'). Question 5: A: "The printer ran out of paper for the survey forms." B: "Don't worry, I ________ and buy some from the store right now." A. am going B. will go C. go D. went Correct Answer: B. will go Explanation: Speaker B makes a spontaneous decision at the exact moment of hearing the problem, which requires 'will'.
